title: A screenshot separated before today only has to be read once more
goal: The app reads the words off every piece of a separated screenshot so the layer rows can say them, and since yesterday it writes that reading into the file so a reopen costs nothing. A file separated before that change does not get the benefit: it reads the whole page again on every open, quietly, and then holds the answer without ever marking the file as needing a save, so unless you happen to save it for some other reason it reads the whole page again next time, and the time after that. Have the first read of an old file stick.
notes:
From the rough list of queue/audits/2026-09-17-what-a-reading-found-is-saved.json: 'A file separated before today opens, reads in the background, and then holds the reading without being marked edited, so the words are only written down if you save for some other reason. A person who never saves it pays the reading again next time.'

Size of the thing being repeated, measured by that same audit on the dense page: 3.1 seconds of CPU over 142 runs, landing as a few hundred milliseconds of background work after every open. Not a stall, which is why this is p3 and not higher, but it is paid forever on a file nobody edits.

The tension to resolve, and it is the whole task: EditorState.applyWithoutMarkingEdited deliberately advances the clean baseline so a reading never makes a file look edited, and that is right. What is missing is a way for a reading of a file that had none to reach the disk without a person being asked. Writing on close, or writing once in the background after the read settles, are both possible and both are a change to when the app touches a file, so say plainly in the audit which one was chosen and why.

Code: Sources/Photonz/EditorState+RunWords.swift, Sources/Photonz/EditorState.swift applyWithoutMarkingEdited, Sources/PhotonzCore/ReadWords.swift, and the reader in PackageIO. Spec: docs/design/separate-reads-the-words.md. Born in commit 4f83fd70.

While in here: the same audit records that a document keeps what was read off a picture even after undo takes that picture out, and nothing ever prunes those entries, so a file separated and undone twenty times carries twenty dead sets of words. Deliberate, a few kilobytes each, and below the follow-up bar on its own; worth a line in this task's audit if it turns out to be free to tidy.
acceptance: Open a document separated before the reading was saved, let the background read finish, close it and open it again: the second open starts no reading at all
The file still does not sprout an edited dot and still does not ask to be saved on close because of a reading
A test covers the old-file path end to end through the same package reader the app uses
The try path: separate a screenshot on a build from before 2026-09-17, save it, then open it on today's build twice. Ships in Next behind next-a-separated-row-says-its-words, which is on by default
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not
